# Results: replication, statistics and calibration of the genome-complexity clock

*Generated by `scripts/make_report.py` from `results/statistics.json` and `results/calibration.json`. Do not edit by hand; run `make reproduce`.*

## 1. Replication

Sharov (2006) printed log10(y) = 8.64 + 0.89x, R² = 0.97, 7.8-fold per Gyr.

| Dataset | n | Intercept | Rate (log10/Gyr) | R² | Fold per Gyr | Origin of 1 bp (Gya) | 95% Fieller | 99% Fieller |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sharov, ages from his Fig. 1 (eukaryotes 2.05, mammals 0.10) | 5 | 8.641 | 0.892 | 0.969 | 7.80 | 9.69 | 7.62 to 13.74 | 6.53 to 22.18 |
| Sharov, Markov et al.'s reprint (2.0, 0.125) | 5 | 8.644 | 0.897 | 0.963 | 7.88 | 9.64 | 7.43 to 14.31 | 6.31 to 25.84 |
| Sharov, mammals at 0 (old repo) | 5 | 8.596 | 0.879 | 0.967 | 7.56 | 9.78 | 7.63 to 14.12 | 6.51 to 23.66 |
| Markov 2010, published ages | 9 | 9.000 | 0.828 | 0.836 | 6.73 | 10.87 | 8.05 to 17.32 | 7.20 to 24.77 |
| Markov 2010, current ages | 9 | 8.873 | 0.753 | 0.738 | 5.66 | 11.79 | 7.99 to 24.15 | 6.96 to 52.13 |
| Extended set, corrected | 13 | 8.760 | 0.804 | 0.770 | 6.37 | 10.89 | 8.26 to 16.49 | 7.54 to 21.18 |

Sharov never prints a data table and gives mammals no date. The ages he plotted (eukaryotes 2.05, mammals 0.10) reproduce all four of his printed statistics; Markov et al.'s reprint (2.0, 0.125) matches the intercept only. Markov et al. report r = 0.914 for their exponential fit (labelled R²); the corresponding R² is 0.836. Updating clade ages to current estimates lowers R² to 0.738 and moves the origin to 11.79 Gya; sampling ages uniformly within current ranges gives a 95% range of 11.41 to 12.18 Gya from age uncertainty alone.

## 2. Within-model uncertainty is small; the straight line itself fails

- **Inside the straight-line model the pre-Earth date is statistically firm.** Even the 99% Fieller interval for Sharov's data starts at 6.53 Gya.
- **York errors-in-variables fit, using the repo's assumed error bars:** Sharov χ² = 2.2 on 3 df (p = 0.52, line acceptable); Markov χ² = 47.4 on 7 df (p = 4.7e-08). **A constant-rate line is rejected for Markov's nine points.**
- **Deming regression** (any ratio of age error to size error) keeps Sharov's origin between 9.43 and 9.69 Gya.
- **Measurement-error route to an Earth origin** (Marzban et al. 2014). Their λ = 1 + σ_w²/σ_b² is the attenuation factor on the slope. A corrected point estimate of 4.5 Gya needs λ = 2.69 (they report "about 2.7"). In a consistent structural model that means an age-error SD of 0.97 to 1.08 Gyr on every clade age, including the mammal point. With σ_b² fixed at the observed 1.86 Gyr², as in their eq. 6, it means 1.77 Gyr, larger than the SD of the dates themselves (1.37). Their own error estimate (σ_w ≈ 0.5 Gyr) gives λ = 1.13, a corrected point estimate near 8.5 Gya; their interval reaching 4.5 Gya rests on a variance term we could not reproduce (see the review, Section 4.1).

## 3. Curve shape: the best-fitting curve has no origin date

| Model (Markov, published ages) | k | RSS | AICc | Origin of 1 bp | Parameter at bound |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| exponential | 3 | 1.715 | -4.12 | 10.87 Gya | no |
| hyperbolic | 3 | 3.555 | 2.44 | none | yes |
| biexponential | 4 | 0.424 | -9.49 | none | no |
| logistic4 | 5 | 0.430 | 2.62 | none | yes |

Of the four curves only the straight line reaches 1 bp. Markov et al.'s own biexponential form fits best and levels off at about 10^6.03 bp in the deep past: it never reaches 1 bp. Models flagged "at bound" are degenerate fits.

A two-segment line breaks at 0.88 Gya with rates 0.43 (older) and 2.57 (younger) log10/Gyr. AICc -12.51 against -4.12 for one line, or -0.51 if the breakpoint is also penalised as a parameter.

## 4. Rate constancy

- Phanerozoic points only: rate 2.57, origin 3.77 Gya. Its predictions for the older points miss by All living beings +6.7, Eukaryotes +2.4, Metazoa +0.8 orders of magnitude.
- Precambrian points only: rate 0.43, origin 18.29 Gya.
- Leave-one-out origins range from 7.04 Gya (dropping All living beings) to 11.37 Gya (dropping Eukaryotes).

## 5. The unobserved interval before the oldest point

Origin = first point age + (its log10 size) / (m × fitted rate). The data fix the fitted rate, not m.

| Anchor | Multiplier m for origin at 4.4 Gya | at 4.5 Gya | Doubling time needed (Myr) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sharov prokaryote, 0.5 Mb at 3.5 Gya | 7.1 | 6.4 | 48 |
| Markov bacterium, 1.3 Mb at 4.0 Gya | 18.5 | 14.8 | 20 |
| LUCA, 2.5 Mb at 4.2 Gya (Moody et al. 2024) | 35.9 | 23.9 | 9 |

Within the observed record, segment rates already differ from the average by factors of 0.52 to 3.11.

The same constant-rate method applied to protein-coding gene counts puts the origin at 20.4 Gya, and to constrained DNA at 16.6 Gya, both older than the universe (13.8).

## 6. Calibration on simulated histories (no clock unless stated)

Life starts at 10^6 bp, 4.0 Gya, so the true origin is on Earth. 25 runs per setting; clade ages are Markov's. Parameters are illustrative.

**A uniform clock is invisible to the method.** In coupled runs (identical random numbers) the nested-minimum slope is 0.516 without a clock and 0.516 with a clock of +0.8 log10/Gyr. The true ancestral series changes from -0.54 to 0.26. Every living genome carries the same total growth, so statistics computed only from living species shift by a constant (this is checked exactly in `tests/test_simulate.py`).

| True clock rate | Method's fitted rate (median) | True ancestral rate (median) | Inferred origin (median, Gya) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.0 | 0.81 | -0.03 | 7.5 |
| 0.4 | 0.89 | 0.39 | 9.1 |
| 0.8 | 0.79 | 0.78 | 11.8 |
| 1.2 | 0.82 | 1.12 | 13.9 |

**No-clock grid** (random focal lineage). Observed Markov slope: 0.83.

| σ | λ | μ | Median tips | Fitted rate (median) | Median R² | Inferred origin | Share inferring pre-Earth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.25 | 1.5 | 0.0 | 241 | 0.28 | 0.91 | 21.2 | 100% |
| 0.25 | 2.0 | 0.0 | 3513 | 0.39 | 0.94 | 15.9 | 100% |
| 0.25 | 2.5 | 0.0 | 9019 | 0.41 | 0.93 | 14.6 | 100% |
| 0.5 | 1.5 | 0.0 | 319 | 0.57 | 0.86 | 11.1 | 100% |
| 0.5 | 2.0 | 0.0 | 2014 | 0.61 | 0.92 | 8.7 | 100% |
| 0.5 | 2.5 | 0.0 | 15250 | 0.86 | 0.94 | 7.4 | 100% |
| 0.75 | 1.5 | 0.0 | 289 | 0.89 | 0.92 | 6.6 | 100% |
| 0.75 | 2.0 | 0.0 | 2750 | 0.88 | 0.94 | 5.7 | 88% |
| 0.75 | 2.5 | 0.0 | 10518 | 1.04 | 0.95 | 5.4 | 72% |
| 1.0 | 1.5 | 0.0 | 442 | 1.57 | 0.90 | 4.7 | 52% |
| 1.0 | 2.0 | 0.0 | 2714 | 1.52 | 0.94 | 4.2 | 44% |
| 1.0 | 2.5 | 0.0 | 12404 | 1.66 | 0.95 | 3.7 | 16% |
| 0.5 | 4.0 | 1.5 | 19340 | 0.84 | 0.94 | 8.6 | 100% |

The share inferring pre-Earth depends on the assumed starting size and on σ and λ. What does not depend on them is that the method reports a positive rate, with high R², when there is no clock at all.

Settings whose no-clock slope is within 0.1 of the observed 0.83 infer a pre-Earth origin in 88% to 100% of runs, with median R² 0.92 to 0.94.

**Choosing the most complex living lineage biases even the true ancestral series.** With no clock, the ancestors of the maximum-genome lineage show median rates of 0.25 to 1.65 log10/Gyr across the grid, because selecting the endpoint selects the path.

With a reflecting floor at 10^5.5 bp (random focal): fitted rate 0.28, median R² 0.72, inferred origin 22.5 Gya.

## 7. Real data (WP3)

Inputs: 17,198 eukaryote species with directly measured genome sizes (GoaT), 50,645-tip Timetree of Life (2015), NCBI taxonomy. Raw files are not redistributed (see `data/external/README.md`); rebuild them with `make fetch`. Sources: GoaT (Challis et al. 2023), TimeTree (Hedges et al. 2015; Kumar et al. 2022), NCBI Taxonomy, GTDB (Parks et al.).

The measured minima match Markov's values closely; the true eukaryote minimum is a parasitic microsporidian. The implied clock depends entirely on which statistic is tracked. Typical genomes barely change between nested clades: the trend lives in the extremes.

### 7.2 Every species as focal lineage, against a no-trend null on the same tree

For each species, the minimum genome size below each of its ancestral nodes is regressed on node age, as in Markov's construction. The null simulates Brownian motion with no trend on the same pruned tree, at the rate estimated by independent contrasts (20 runs).

| Tree | Tips | σ (log10/√Gyr) | Observed rate, median (IQR) | Observed R² | Null rate, median of runs (range) | Null R² | Share pre-Earth: observed / null |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Eukaryota | 5,212 | 1.42 | 1.26 (1.05 to 1.63) | 0.90 | 2.20 (1.48 to 3.19) | 0.79 | 94% / 18% |
| Metazoa | 2,362 | 0.55 | 1.56 (1.34 to 1.86) | 0.89 | 1.25 (0.65 to 2.38) | 0.86 | 87% / 98% |
| Viridiplantae | 2,708 | 1.90 | 1.31 (1.12 to 1.78) | 0.71 | 3.63 (1.69 to 6.06) | 0.69 | 80% / 2% |

In animals the observed rates fall inside the no-trend range. In plants the Brownian null overshoots, because whole-genome duplications inflate the rate estimate; the observed plant rates are lower than a trendless random walk would give, which is the opposite of what a clock would add.

**Different lineages imply different origins.** Median implied origin by focal clade:

| Focal clade | Focal species | Median rate | Median implied origin (Gya) | IQR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Viridiplantae | 2,708 | 1.09 | 7.8 | 6.8 to 8.4 |
| Fungi | 97 | 0.45 | 16.4 | 15.6 to 17.9 |
| Metazoa | 2,362 | 1.54 | 6.0 | 5.5 to 6.5 |
| Arthropoda | 275 | 1.03 | 8.3 | 6.5 to 8.8 |
| Vertebrata | 1,995 | 1.58 | 5.9 | 5.5 to 6.4 |
| Mammalia | 399 | 1.73 | 5.5 | 5.4 to 5.7 |

A universal clock would give one date. These span 11.0 Gyr (5.5 to 16.4 Gya); estimates above 13.8 are older than the universe.

## 8. Prokaryotes: has the genome grown since LUCA? (WP3)

GTDB v232: species representatives; CheckM2 completeness >= 95%, contamination <= 5%; size / completeness. LUCA estimate: 2.49 to 2.99 Mb about 4.2 Gya (Moody et al. 2024).

| Set | Species | 5% | Median | 95% | Max | Share smaller than LUCA (2.49 / 2.99 Mb) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bacteria, all | 88,346 | 1.01 | 3.61 | 7.92 | 16.23 | 25% / 36% |
| Bacteria, isolates | 35,359 | 1.89 | 4.35 | 9.05 | 14.24 | 13% / 20% |
| Archaea, all | 2,613 | 0.97 | 2.03 | 4.27 | 6.53 | 65% / 76% |
| Archaea, isolates | 909 | 1.54 | 3.12 | 4.67 | 5.99 | 34% / 47% |
| All prokaryote isolates | 36,268 | 1.86 | 4.31 | 9.02 | 14.24 | 13% / 21% |

LUCA's genome sits inside the modern range. Growth from LUCA to the median modern isolate implies 0.056 log10/Gyr, a doubling about every 5.4 Gyr, against Sharov's 0.89 (every 0.34 Gyr). Across 4.2 Gyr of prokaryotic evolution the typical genome has changed little, as Koonin argued in 2006. This does not exclude growth followed by reduction, but it leaves no room for a steady clock in the prokaryotic era.

## 9. What this means for the next stages

1. Statistics built only from living species (clade minima, maxima, representatives) cannot measure a uniform clock. Their slope reflects trait spread and diversification, and on the real animal tree a no-trend model reproduces the observed slopes.
2. The same argument means extant-only reconstructions on a time-calibrated tree cannot identify a uniform trend either, since every tip has evolved for the same time. WP4 needs fossil genome-size proxies or gene-family histories, which carry information about the past directly.
3. Focal lineages must be chosen without regard to their genome size, or the selection must be modelled.
4. Brownian motion fits plants poorly (whole-genome duplications inflate the rate). Bounded and jump models (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, Lévy) are the next null models to fit.
